name: DeepSpeed-MoE: Advancing Mixture-of-Experts Inference and Training to Power Next-Generation AI Scale
problem: MoE's training cost saving did not carry over to serving, because inference keeps all experts resident and pays an all-to-all every layer, so a dense model can be cheaper per token to serve.
mechanism: End-to-end MoE training and inference system inside DeepSpeed with three separable contributions. (a) MoE architecture variants, including a DeepSeekMoE-style fine-grained expert split plus a shared expert that every token passes through, absorbing common knowledge and reducing routed load. (b) Model compression shrinking MoE models by up to 3.7x using expert pruning of below-average-importance experts alongside distillation, so the resident expert set shrinks rather than only the per-token compute; this is the genuinely novel and rarely copied part. (c) An inference kernel path that groups tokens into fixed-size buffers before dispatch, so the all-to-all becomes a few large bursty transfers instead of many small ones. Load balancing is the auxiliary-loss kind typical of this period.
speedup_reported: 7.3x better latency and cost than existing MoE inference solutions (the comparison set is prior MoE serving systems, not a dense model); MoE model size reduced by up to 3.7x via expert pruning plus distillation; and, for serving up to massive MoE models, up to 4.5x faster and 9x cheaper inference than quality-equivalent dense models. Also restates a 5x training cost saving for autoregressive LMs versus quality-equivalent dense models, which the paper attributes to shared work with GShard and Switch rather than to DeepSpeed-MoE alone. Measured on V100 and A100-class GPUs.
notes:
DeepSpeed ships the MoE layer and is a real upstream inference path, so the system is in-upstream-engine; the numbers themselves are DeepSpeed's own. Title text differs across arXiv versions: earlier versions read 'Advancing Mixture-of-Experts Inference and Training for Power-Scale Deep Learning'. The shared-expert idea from (a) became the standard recipe via DeepSeek; the expert-pruning-plus-distillation idea from (b) was largely not copied.
